Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, during the presentation, the listen-only mode will be in effect. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star one one on your telephone keypad. We ask that while you pose your question, you keep it to one question and one follow-up. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q2 FY2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; Dr. Elena Vasquez, CTO; Jordan Lee, Chief Revenue Officer; and Lisa Wong, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Actual results may differ materially due to a variety of factors. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q2 FY2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on six key areas: operating margin, sales efficiency, average contract value or ACV, MRR trends, operating expense breakdown, and cash runway. These metrics highlight the scalability of our business model and our ability to deliver profitable growth in a dynamic SaaS environment.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss the financials in more detail.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $248 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82.4%, and operating income was $45.1 million, reflecting an operating margin of 18.2%.

Let me start by focusing on our operating margin, which came in at 18.2% for the quarter. This represents a 320 basis point expansion year-over-year from 15.0% in Q2 FY2023, and a sequential improvement of 220 basis points from 16.0% in Q1 FY2024. This marks our sixth consecutive quarter of operating margin expansion, underscoring the scalability of our SaaS model as we continue to execute on our Rule of 40+ strategy—delivering 28% year-over-year revenue growth while maintaining strong free cash flow margins north of 25%.

The key drivers behind this performance begin with top-line tailwinds. Revenue growth outpaced our operating expenses by a 3:1 ratio, providing natural operating leverage. Our net revenue retention or NRR stood at 118%, fueled by upsells in our core ForgeAI platform, which now powers over 65% of our customer workflows. Large deals over $1 million ACV accelerated 45% year-over-year, including a multi-year deployment with a Fortune 50 financial services firm for AI-driven contract automation, akin to the Salesforce Einstein expansions we've seen industry-wide. Our dollar-based net expansion rate held steady at 125% for customers with over $100K ARR, reflecting sticky usage in our low-code/no-code modules amid the ongoing developer productivity boom.

On sales and marketing efficiency, S&M expenses as a percentage of revenue declined to 32% from 38% a year ago, a 600 basis point improvement. This was propelled by our shift toward product-led growth or PLG initiatives, where self-serve adoption via our freemium tier drove 22% of new ARR bookings—reducing customer acquisition costs or CAC by 15% to $4,200 per customer. Payback periods compressed to 14 months from 18 months, outperforming peers like HubSpot in their recent quarters. Regionally, this leverage was strongest in North America, which accounts for 85% of revenue, where mature sales teams achieved 35% YoY quota attainment. In EMEA, which grew 42% YoY to 12% of total revenue, we benefited from lighter variable comp structures post-Brexit normalization, though we continue investing in localized go-to-market for GDPR-compliant verticals like healthcare.

Cost of revenue discipline helped amid cloud pressures. Gross margin expanded 180 basis points despite a 10-12% uptick in AWS and Azure hosting costs tied to broader cloud inflation—echoing what Snowflake reported in their Q1 with multi-tenant inefficiencies. We offset this through technical optimizations: migrating 40% of our workload to our proprietary ForgeEdge serverless architecture, which reduced data egress fees by 25% and improved GPU utilization for AI inference by 30%. Third-party support costs also declined 8% as a percent of revenue, thanks to proactive churn mitigation via our Customer Success AI playbooks, keeping dollar churn under 1% for the fifth straight quarter.

R&D investments are yielding long-term leverage. R&D came in at 18% of revenue, flat YoY, as we prioritized high-ROI projects like integrating open-source LLMs such as Llama 3 fine-tuning into our platform for zero-shot automation—mirroring Adobe's Firefly strategy. This not only boosted NRR but also positioned us ahead of the curve in the agentic AI wave, with early pilots showing 3x productivity gains for enterprise devs. We're ahead of the pack here compared to Workday's measured AI ramp, and these initiatives are already contributing to a 15% reduction in engineering toil via automated testing pipelines.

G&A and regional headwinds were mitigated. G&A held steady at 14% of revenue, with share-based comp dilution minimized to 2.5% through our refreshed equity refresh program. APAC, now 3% of revenue but growing 60% YoY, presented a margin headwind due to upfront localization costs for Japan and India markets—similar to ServiceNow's playbook—but we expect breakeven on these investments by Q4 as ARR ramps. Macro tailwinds like stabilizing tech spend, per Bessemer Cloud Index, helped, though we remain vigilant on forex volatility impacting our 15% non-USD revenue exposure.

Looking ahead, we guide to Q3 operating margin of 19-20%, implying continued expansion toward our long-term target of 25%+ by FY2026. This trajectory assumes sustained NRR above 115%, PLG scaling to 30% of bookings, and cloud cost optimizations via multi-cloud hedging. In a SaaS landscape where median operating margins hover at 12-15% per KeyBanc data, our outperformance stems from our asset-light model, AI moat, and sales productivity—putting us in the upper quartile alongside leaders like Atlassian.

Next, on sales efficiency, which remains a cornerstone of our go-to-market strategy here at CloudForge. In the SaaS landscape, where customer acquisition costs can average $1.20 to $1.50 per dollar of new ARR according to the latest Bessemer Cloud Index, optimizing sales cycles and conversion rates is critical to driving Rule of 40 performance and shortening payback periods. We're pleased to report continued strong progress on both fronts in Q2, with meaningful improvements that position us ahead of industry medians.

Our quarter-end weighted average sales cycle across the business stood at 7.2 months, down 12% year-over-year from 8.2 months in Q2 last year. This acceleration is driven by a multi-pronged approach we've been executing since our Q4 2023 sales reset. For context, enterprise deals—those with ACV over $200K, which comprised 42% of our new bookings—averaged 8.9 months, a 15% reduction YoY, thanks to our expanded self-service trial capabilities and AI-assisted proof-of-concept or PoC environments. We're now delivering customized PoCs in under two weeks using our ForgeAI demo engine, which automates workflow simulations tailored to prospects' ERP data—similar to the personalization tech that's helped Snowflake shave months off their cycles post-2023.

Mid-market segments, ACV $50K-$200K, clocked in at 4.1 months, flat sequentially but up 8% in velocity YoY, fueled by our partner ecosystem with integrators like Celigo and Boomi. And in SMB/self-serve, where PLG is king, cycles are sub-30 days at just 22 days—over 20% faster than the SaaS average benchmarked by OpenView Partners—reflecting viral adoption of our freemium tier, now at 150K+ active users.

Regionally, we're seeing divergence worth noting. In North America, which drove 62% of Q2 bookings, cycles tightened to 6.8 months on stronger inbound from our revamped content engine, generating 3x more MQLs via SEO-optimized resources on composable architecture—a hot topic amid the low-code/no-code boom. EMEA held steady at 8.1 months, but we're targeting sub-8 by year-end through localized sales plays, like our recent DACH-focused bundle with SAP integrations, addressing GDPR hurdles that have plagued peers like UiPath. APAC, at 7.9 months, improved 18% YoY despite macro headwinds; our Tokyo storefront launch and partnerships with NTT Data are converting faster in Japan, where enterprise diligence remains elongated.

Shifting to conversion rates, our funnel efficiency is equally robust. Overall SQL-to-close win rate hit 32% in Q2, up from 28% YoY and above our 30% internal target—putting us in the top quartile per SaaS Metrics benchmarks. Drilling down: MQL-to-SQL conversion improved to 24%, a 4-point gain, propelled by our GenAI lead scoring model in Salesforce, which prioritizes intent signals from 50+ data sources, boosting precision by 35% and reducing sales rep touch time on low-propensity leads. SQL-to-demo conversion leaped to 68% from 62%, as our virtual seller tool—think Gong meets Chorus.ai with real-time objection handling—has cut no-show rates by 40%.

Opportunity-to-close closed the loop at 28% for enterprise (31% mid-market), with expansions playing an outsized role: 45% of our Q2 net new ARR came from existing logos, a testament to our land-and-expand playbook. Magic quadrant momentum helped here—our latest Gartner positioning drove a 15% uplift in close rates against ServiceNow competitors. Notably, win rates against point solutions like Zapier dipped to 75% in mid-market, but we're countering with deeper MuleSoft-like API marketplace integrations.

These metrics translate to tangible efficiency: Q2 sales efficiency ratio—new ARR per sales rep—reached $1.42M, up 22% YoY, with CAC payback now at 14 months enterprise-wide, down from 18. Rule of 40 aside, this supports our 1.3x bookings growth target for FY24.

Strategically, we're doubling down on three initiatives: First, rolling out ForgeAI Sales Copilot company-wide in Q3, aiming for another 10-15% cycle compression by automating 60% of discovery calls. Second, accelerating PLG with usage-based pricing tiers, targeting 40% self-serve ARR mix by mid-2025—inspired by HubSpot's evolution. Third, regional specialization: dedicating 20% more AE bandwidth to high-velocity APAC verticals like fintech, where we've seen 35% better conversions post our Stripe Atlas tie-in.

Looking forward, we guide to sales cycles of 7.0 months in Q3 and win rates holding 31-33%, supporting $185M-$195M in Q3 bookings. This efficiency edge, amid a SaaS market still grappling with 15-20% median contraction per Synergy Research, underscores CloudForge's resilience and path to 25%+ free cash flow margins by FY25.

Turning to average contract value or ACV, which represents the annualized revenue per customer contract, calculated as the total contract value divided by the number of contracts, normalized to a 12-month equivalent. This metric is a leading indicator of our land-and-expand strategy, pricing discipline, and customer stickiness in a market where enterprise buyers are increasingly consolidating vendors amid economic headwinds.

In Q2 FY2024, our overall ACV came in at $52,300, marking a strong 22% year-over-year increase from $42,800 in Q2 FY2023, and a sequential 7% rise from $48,900 in Q1 FY2024. This acceleration reflects not just top-of-funnel demand but genuine depth in deal construction, with net revenue retention holding steady at 118%—a testament to our ability to upsell and cross-sell within our ecosystem.

Breaking it down by customer segment: Enterprise deals over $100k ACV, now 42% of our total ACV mix up from 35% a year ago, delivered an ACV of $168,000—up 28% YoY. Key driver here is multi-year commitments tied to our ForgeAI suite, which integrates generative AI for sales forecasting and customer 360 insights. We've seen deals mirroring Salesforce's Einstein expansions, with customers like a Fortune 500 retailer bundling our core CRM with ForgeAI and DataForge analytics for a 35% ACV uplift on average. Land-and-expand is working: 65% of these wins included expansions from existing logos.

Mid-market, $25k-$100k ACV, grew 19% YoY to $62,500, comprising 38% of the mix. This cohort benefits from our partner ecosystem—think integrations with Microsoft Dynamics and Snowflake—enabling faster time-to-value. A notable trend is pricing optimization via usage-based tiers, which added 12% to ACV through overage revenue recognition.

SMB under $25k ACV at $12,400, up 8% YoY, remains our volume driver at 20% of the mix. While growth is more modest, it's fueled by self-serve adoption of our starter packs, with 25% converting to paid add-ons like mobile-first apps within the first quarter.

Regionally, North America, 72% of ACV, at $58,200, up 25% YoY, propelled by hyperscaler partnerships—our AWS Marketplace listing drove a 40% ACV bump in deals co-sold with Amazon Bedrock for AI workloads. Economic resilience here, post-Fed rate cuts, has enterprises like regional banks prioritizing AI consolidation over cost-cutting.

EMEA, 18% of ACV, surged 30% YoY to $45,600, our fastest-growing region. GDPR-compliant ForgeAI features have resonated, with wins in financial services mirroring Workday's EMEA traction. However, FX headwinds shaved 2 points off reported growth.

APAC, 10% of ACV, at $38,900, up 15% YoY but sequentially flat due to Japan enterprise deal scrutiny amid yen volatility. Strategic wins include a telco giant in Singapore adopting our full stack, boosting local ACV by 22%.

What’s driving these trends? Our Q1-launched ForgeAI platform has been a game-changer—early adopters see 3x ROI on sales pipeline accuracy, per our IDC-validated benchmarks, justifying premium pricing. We've also refined our sales motions: 55% of Q2 ACV came from multi-product deals, up from 42% YoY, leveraging API-first architecture for seamless upsells. Pricing power remains intact—no broad discounts, with 18% of deals carrying 10%+ list-price premiums for strategic bundles. Macro tailwinds include SaaS market recovery; per Gartner, enterprise SaaS spend is rebounding to 12% CAGR through 2028, favoring platforms like ours with 99.99% uptime SLAs.

Strategically, we're doubling down on vertical-specific ACV playbooks—e.g., healthcare modules compliant with HIPAA, targeting $200k+ ACV; channel acceleration, where resellers like Accenture contribute 22% of enterprise ACV; and consumption-linked expansions, piloting flexible pricing akin to Snowflake's model to capture upside as AI usage scales.

Looking ahead, we guide Q3 FY2024 ACV to $54,000-$56,000, implying 20-24% YoY growth, assuming stable FX and continued AI momentum. Risks include elongated enterprise sales cycles in APAC, but our 125% dollar-based net expansion rate positions us well. This ACV trajectory reinforces CloudForge's premium positioning in a crowded SaaS landscape—we're not just growing bookings; we're building durable revenue moats.

Now, on MRR trends, which continue to be the bedrock of our SaaS financial model here at CloudForge. Monthly Recurring Revenue—or MRR—is our north star metric, reflecting the predictable, high-quality revenue stream from our cloud-native DevOps platform, serving over 12,000 customers building and deploying software at scale.

We ended the quarter with $45.2 million in ending MRR, representing 28% year-over-year growth—that's up from 25% in Q1 and 22% in Q4 FY2023, marking a clear acceleration in our topline momentum. Sequentially, MRR grew 8.1% quarter-over-quarter, outpacing our historical average of 7% and beating our internal guide of 7-8%. This puts us on track for full-year FY2024 MRR growth of approximately 26-27%, even as we lap tougher comps from last year's post-pandemic surge.

To unpack the significant changes, new logo acquisition contributed $4.8 million in new annualized MRR, or about 13% sequential growth in this bucket. This was fueled by our "Forge Accelerate" sales motion, where we targeted mid-market teams migrating from legacy tools like Jenkins or on-prem Bamboo setups. We added 450 net new logos, with average contract value for new enterprise deals hitting $185K ARR—a 15% increase YoY—thanks to bundling our new AI-Driven Pipeline Optimizer, which has seen 40% attach rates in pilots. Geographically, Americas drove 55% of new MRR at $2.6M, EMEA chipped in 30% or $1.4M amid strong demand from UK fintechs and German auto suppliers optimizing CI/CD for EV software stacks, while APAC grew to 15% share at $700K, up from 10% last quarter, propelled by partnerships with Alibaba Cloud and wins in Singapore's sovereign tech ecosystem.

Expansion revenue was the standout at $5.2 million, representing 11.5% sequential growth and 42% of total MRR add. Our dollar-based net expansion rate or DBNER expanded to 118% for the quarter—up 200 basis points from Q1's 116%—highlighting sticky land-and-expand dynamics. Key here: upsells from existing customers adopting our GenAI features, like AutoScale Predictor, which dynamically rightsizes compute resources akin to what Harness or GitLab are pushing. We saw 320 expansion deals, averaging 25% pod size increase, particularly in our top 100 customers cohort, where NRR hit 125%. A great example is our flagship customer, a top-5 hyperscaler, who expanded by $1.2M MRR after integrating our platform with their Kubernetes orchestrator for edge deployments.

On the flip side, churn and contraction remained disciplined at 4.2% gross dollar churn—flat QoQ and well below the SaaS industry median of 5-7% per Benchmarkit data—and 89% logo retention, with non-renewals concentrated in low-ACV SMBs facing macro squeeze. Contraction MRR was $1.9M, or 4.1% of beginning MRR, primarily from pricing fatigue in cost-sensitive EMEA SMBs, where inflation hit 8% YoY. We've countered this with our Q1 pricing optimization—selective 5-10% uplifts on premium tiers—which added $800K to MRR without material pushback, mirroring strategies at Snowflake and Datadog.

Regionally, Americas MRR grew 26% YoY to $28.5M (63% of total), steady as she goes with robust enterprise demand. EMEA accelerated to 32% YoY growth at $10.8M (24% share), outpacing the region thanks to GDPR-compliant AI tooling resonating with EU regulators. APAC was the rocket at 42% YoY to $5.9M (13% share), driven by Japan and India ramps—think wins with SoftBank portfolio companies shifting from CircleCI amid yen volatility.

Strategically, these trends validate our "AI Everywhere" pivot. Post our June launch of ForgeAI Suite, we've seen 25% faster sales cycles and 15% higher win rates against incumbents like Atlassian Bamboo or Azure DevOps. We're doubling down with $50M in FY25 R&D for agentic workflows, targeting 120% NRR in our top cohorts. That said, we're not immune to headwinds: elongated sales cycles in a high-interest environment have pushed some SMB deals into Q3, and currency FX—particularly a 5% euro headwind—shaved 100bps off reported growth. Mitigations include hedging 80% of EMEA exposure and our "Freemium-to-Paid" flywheel, which converted 18% of Q2 trials.

In summary, MRR's 28% YoY growth with accelerating components underscores our competitive moat in a $50B+ DevOps market growing at 20% CAGR per Gartner. We're raising our FY24 ending MRR guide to $48-49M, implying 27% growth.

Before I move to guidance, a quick look at operating expense breakdown. Total operating expenses came in at $120 million for the quarter, up 15% year-over-year, but importantly, down 200 basis points as a percentage of revenue to 80% from 82% a year ago. This reflects our ongoing shift toward operating leverage as we scale beyond $600 million in annual run-rate revenue. Non-GAAP adjustments, primarily for $18 million in stock-based compensation and $4 million in acquisition-related amortization, bring our adjusted op-ex to $98 million.

Research and development: $36 million, up 20% YoY, or 24% of total op-ex (flat YoY as a mix). R&D remains our largest investment area at 24% of revenue, underscoring our commitment to product leadership in the enterprise collaboration and AI analytics space. This quarter's spend was driven by accelerating our GenAI roadmap. We've doubled down on proprietary large language models integrated into CloudForge Analytics, similar to what Snowflake did with Cortex or Databricks with its MosaicML acquisition. This includes $12 million in cloud compute costs for training on hyperscaler infrastructure like AWS SageMaker and Azure OpenAI, plus hiring 45 engineers focused on multimodal AI for real-time data visualization and natural language querying. Early results are promising: beta users report 40% faster insight generation, which is already contributing to a 15% uptick in net revenue retention from our top 500 customers.

Second, cybersecurity enhancements amid rising threats—we allocated $5 million to zero-trust architecture upgrades and quantum-resistant encryption, aligning with industry standards post the Okta breach headlines. Regionally, 60% of R&D spend remains in North America, but we're ramping up our Bangalore center, now at 25% of headcount, to tap lower-cost talent for foundational ML work while keeping core IP in the U.S. Looking ahead, we expect R&D to grow in the mid-teens percentage-wise, but as a percentage of revenue, it should decline to 22% by year-end as AI efficiencies compound—think fewer engineers needed for routine features thanks to tools like GitHub Copilot Enterprise.

Sales and marketing: $54 million, up 12% YoY, or 45% of total op-ex (down 300 bps YoY as a mix). Sales and marketing marked a deliberate moderation in growth, reflecting improved efficiency with our magic number now at 1.4—up from 1.1 last year—indicating strong return on incremental spend. Customer acquisition cost payback compressed to 16 months from 19, driven by our product-led growth motion. Freemium upsells now account for 35% of new ARR, mirroring successes at companies like HubSpot or Notion, reducing reliance on field sales.

We invested $20 million in demand generation, with 40% shifting to high-ROI digital channels: LinkedIn campaigns targeting Fortune 1000 CISOs yielded a 4x pipeline multiple, while SEO and content around 'AI-driven collaboration analytics' boosted organic traffic 50% YoY. Sales headcount grew just 8% to 350 reps, with a focus on mid-market expansion via our CloudForge One bundle—priced at $99/user/month, it's resonating in SMBs facing Microsoft Teams fatigue. Regionally, North America drove 70% of spend but only 55% of new logos, as EMEA grew to 25% of bookings (up from 18%) through localized go-to-market in London and Frankfurt. APAC remains nascent at 10%, but partnerships with Alibaba Cloud are accelerating trials there. Strategically, we're optimizing by rightsizing underperforming teams—post-Q1 restructuring, sales productivity is up 22%—and leaning into partner ecosystems like the AWS Marketplace, where 20% of Q2 deals originated. Expect S&M to grow at high-single digits, dipping to 40% of op-ex mix by FYE.

General and administrative: $30 million, up 10% YoY, or 25% of total op-ex (down 100 bps YoY as a mix). G&A came in efficiently at 20% of revenue—down from 22% YoY—demonstrating the leverage from our $600 million revenue base. Primary drivers included $8 million in stock-based comp for retaining key executives amid the talent wars, and $6 million in legal/compliance for GDPR expansions and SOC 2 Type II recertification. Headcount here grew minimally at 5%, with automation via tools like Workday Adaptive Planning cutting finance cycle times by 30%. No major M&A this quarter, but we're carrying $3 million in integration costs from last year's Fusion Analytics tuck-in. Regionally, EMEA compliance added $2 million due to evolving data sovereignty rules, but our shared services model in the Philippines keeps costs flat. Overall, G&A should remain range-bound as a percentage of revenue, supporting margin expansion toward 30% adjusted EBITDA by FY2025.

Our op-ex profile reflects a maturing SaaS leader: heavy R&D for defensibility in an AI arms race, efficient S&M fueling 120%+ net dollar retention, and lean G&A enabling scale. This positions us well against peers like ServiceNow or Workday, even as macro headwinds linger in discretionary IT spend.

Finally, on our liquidity position and cash runway, which remain a cornerstone of our financial health. As of the end of Q2 FY2024, our consolidated cash, cash equivalents, and short-term marketable securities stood at $452 million, up 8% sequentially from $418 million at the end of Q1. This positions us exceptionally well, providing a robust 20-month cash runway at our current trailing twelve-month net cash burn rate of approximately $27 million per quarter, or $108 million annualized. For context, this burn rate reflects a 15% year-over-year improvement, driven by our disciplined operating leverage initiatives and accelerating revenue momentum.

In Q2, we generated $18 million in operating cash flow, a $12 million sequential improvement and our second consecutive quarter of positive cash flow from operations. This was fueled by a 128% dollar-based net revenue retention rate—ahead of peers like HubSpot's recent 107% and well above the industry average of 110%—as our AI-powered upsell engine, particularly within Nexlify Analytics Pro, captured expanding workloads from existing customers. Free cash flow came in at negative $5 million, or -2% of revenue, a 1,200 basis point improvement YoY, thanks to capex discipline; we're now running at under 4% of revenue on property and equipment, focused primarily on GPU-intensive AI training clusters in AWS and Azure for our next-gen predictive modeling features.

Our cash burn has trended downward consistently: Q1 burn was $35 million, Q2 $27 million. This trajectory is supported by revenue acceleration and RPO visibility: Q2 ARR grew 32% YoY to $285 million, with remaining performance obligations or RPO at $620 million, up 45% YoY and representing 2.2x our ARR. Current RPO—our multi-year committed backlog—grew 55% YoY, signaling strong demand for our platform amid the generative AI boom. Enterprise wins like our $15 million multi-year deal with a Fortune 100 retailer underscore this, mirroring tailwinds seen at Snowflake with their AI Data Cloud ramp.

Cost optimization initiatives have realized $45 million in annualized run-rate savings from our 2023 restructuring, including a 22% reduction in non-AI engineering headcount through automation and offshoring select QA functions to Eastern Europe. Go-to-market efficiency is improving, with sales and marketing at 48% of revenue (down from 55% YoY), as we lean into product-led growth via freemium tiers for our Nexlify Flow orchestrator, akin to successful plays by Notion and Linear.

Technical and infrastructure efficiencies: our migration to Kubernetes-orchestrated microservices has cut cloud costs by 28%, with committed use discounts on GCP yielding $8 million in savings. We're also optimizing AI inference costs—critical in SaaS—by fine-tuning our LLMs on proprietary customer data, reducing token throughput expenses by 40% compared to off-the-shelf models like those from OpenAI.

Regionally, our cash position supports aggressive expansion. North America remains 78% of ARR but grew 28% YoY, while EMEA surged 52% on GDPR-compliant features that resonated with DACH enterprises, outpacing Salesforce's regional growth. APAC is our fastest grower at 65% YoY, bolstered by a new Tokyo data center and partnerships with Tencent Cloud, though forex headwinds from a strengthening USD shaved 2 points off growth there.

Strategically, this runway gives us ample flexibility to invest without dilution in high-ROI areas: $50 million earmarked for FY2024 in agentic AI R&D (think autonomous workflow agents competing with UiPath and Zapier), customer success expansions to push NRR toward 135%, and potential tuck-in M&A like last year's $120 million acquisition of a vertical SaaS player in healthcare analytics. In today's high-interest-rate environment—where VC dry powder is down 30% YoY per PitchBook—our path to FCF positivity by H2 FY2025 positions us favorably against cash-burning peers like Datadog or Monday.com.

We're not complacent; our board-approved capital allocation framework prioritizes organic growth, with any future financing opportunistic and at favorable terms. With $452 million in the bank and burn under control, CloudForge is built to weather macro uncertainty and capitalize on the $200 billion+ SaaS TAM expansion driven by AI adoption.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first half of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $950 million to $975 million.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez for a technology update.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mike. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers, including zero-trust upgrades and optimizations for multi-cloud environments that have reduced latency by 25% for global deployments.

And now Lisa Wong will provide an update on the product roadmap.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Elena. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of ForgeAI Sales Copilot. This new feature significantly improves sales productivity by automating discovery calls and lead scoring, delivering 3x faster PoCs and higher win rates. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature, which aligns with our product strategy to embed AI everywhere across the customer journey.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. As a reminder, to ask a question, please press star one one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, and how it compares to your initial expectations?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Ben. ForgeAI has been transformative for our growth, contributing over 40% of new ARR in Q2 through high attach rates of 65% in existing customer expansions and 45% in new enterprise deals over $1M ACV. This has accelerated NRR to 118% and driven 28% overall revenue growth. Compared to initial expectations, we're ahead by 15-20% on adoption velocity, especially in North America and EMEA, where it's powering upsells similar to Salesforce Einstein, validating our land-and-expand model.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Kumar with Morgan Stanley.

Priya Kumar:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, and what are your key target markets?

Sarah Chen:
Great question, Priya. International expansion remains a priority, with APAC growing 60% YoY to 13% of revenue and MRR. Our plans include ramping localization in Japan and India via partnerships like NTT Data and Alibaba Cloud, targeting fintech, telcos, and sovereign tech—key markets like Singapore and Tokyo where we've secured wins boosting ACV by 22%. We're investing in Tokyo data centers and GDPR-equivalent compliance for faster cycles, aiming for APAC to hit 20% of revenue by FY2026, building on 42% YoY MRR growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lopez with JPMorgan.

David Lopez:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, and what are your strategies to improve customer retention?

Mike Patel:
Thanks, David. Churn remains low at 4.2% gross dollar churn, flat QoQ and below industry medians, concentrated in low-ACV SMBs. NRR trends are strong at 118% overall, expanding to 125% in top cohorts and 128% dollar-based, driven by AI upsells like ForgeAI. Retention strategies include Customer Success AI playbooks reducing churn under 1%, pricing optimizations adding $800K MRR, freemium conversions at 18%, and vertical playbooks—keeping logo retention at 89% amid macro pressures.
